Deprecated: extract shocks via Kalman filter

Source: R/kfpredict.R
kfpredict.Rd

kfpredict() has been renamed to predict_shocks(). It is kept for backward compatibility, issues a deprecation warning and will be removed in a future release.

Usage

kfpredict(Sig, SigR, Psi, et, tol = sqrt(.Machine$double.eps), scale = TRUE)

Arguments

Sig

Numeric matrix (M x M, with M = N for one horizon). Covariance matrix of the residuals in et on policy event days (e.g. Sig from hetiv()).

SigR

Numeric matrix (M x M). Covariance matrix of the residuals on control (non-event) days. Used to back out the implied shock variances when scale = TRUE.

Psi

Numeric matrix (M x E) of responses of the residuals in et to the E structural shocks (e.g. Psi from hetiv()), or an array N x E x M of responses at M horizons, which is stacked by rows.

et

Numeric matrix or data frame (T x M) of forecast errors on event days (e.g. et from hetiv()), or an array T x N x M of forecast errors at M horizons, which is stacked by columns. Rows correspond to time periods.

tol

Numeric scalar. Tolerance for the generalized inverse (MASS::ginv()). Clipped from below at sqrt(.Machine$double.eps).

scale

Logical. If TRUE (default), shocks are rescaled to unit variance using the implied shock variances recovered from Sig and SigR. This scaling assumes that structural shock variances are diagonal, so that Sig - SigR = sum_i sigma_i Psi_i Psi_i'. If FALSE, the raw Kalman filter projection is returned.

Value

See predict_shocks().
